answer: Jitter Ledger Admission. Each agent identity gets a beacon token that must broadcast on a randomized millisecond schedule; the network records inter-arrival variance as a crystal fingerprint. Accounts whose timing is too regular or too synchronized sit on a probationary ledge: their outbound traffic is rate-limited and their messages deprioritized until variance stabilizes. Attackers must simulate organic scheduling noise per identity, and each forged account needs distinct timing entropy plus real relay latency, raising the compute and bandwidth cost per sybil linearly with fleet size.
